title.zh: 卷461 列傳二百四十八 宋庆 吕本元 徐邦道 马玉昆 依克唐阿 荣和 长顺
title.en: Volume 461 Biographies 248: Song Qing, Lv Benyuan, Xu Bangdao, Ma Yukun, Yi Ke Tang A, Rong He, Zhang Shun
title.raw: 卷461 列傳二百四十八 宋庆 吕本元 徐邦道 马玉昆 依克唐阿 荣和 长顺

sentences.zh: 列傳二百四十八

translations.literal: Biographies 248
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 248

sentences.zh: 宋慶呂本元徐邦道馬玉昆依克唐阿榮和長順宋慶，字祝三，山東萊州人。

translations.literal: Song Qing, Lü Benyuan, Xu Bangdao, Ma Yukun, I Ketang'a, Rong He, Zhang Shun — Song Qing, styled Zhushan, was a native of Laizhou, Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qing, Lü Benyuan, Xu Bangdao, Ma Yukun, I Ketang'a, Rong He, and Zhang Shun — Song Qing, whose style was Zhushan, came from Laizhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 家貧落魄，聞同里宮國勳知亳州，往依為奴。

translations.literal: His family was poor and he was in reduced circumstances; hearing that Gong Guoxun of his native place had become prefect of Bozhou, he went to rely on him as a servant.
translations.idiomatic: Born poor and without prospects, he learned that a fellow townsman, Gong Guoxun, had been appointed prefect of Bozhou and went there to enter his service as a household retainer.

sentences.zh: 亳捻孫之友偽就撫，慶察其意叵測，請擊之。

translations.literal: A Nian rebel from Bozhou, Sun Zhiyou, feigned acceptance of pacification; Song Qing perceived his intentions were unpredictable and requested to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When a Nian chieftain from Bozhou named Sun Zhiyou pretended to submit to government pacification, Song Qing saw through his unreliable intentions and asked permission to strike him.

sentences.zh: 國勳壯其志，署為州練長。

translations.literal: Gong Guoxun admired his spirit and appointed him head of the prefectural militia training.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Guoxun was impressed by his resolve and named him head of the prefecture's militia drill corps.

sentences.zh: 之友降，遂接統其眾，號奇勝營，薦授千總。

translations.literal: When Zhiyou surrendered, he then took over command of his forces, styled the battalion Qisheng, and was recommended for appointment as battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhiyou surrendered, Song Qing absorbed his troops under a new unit called the Qisheng Battalion and was recommended for promotion to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 自是守宿州，剿豫匪，釋鳳陽圍，保徐、泗後路。

translations.literal: From then on he garrisoned Suzhou, suppressed bandits in Henan, lifted the siege of Fengyang, and secured the rear routes of Xuzhou and Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he held Suzhou, hunted bandits in Henan, broke the siege of Fengyang, and kept the lines of communication open behind Xuzhou and Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 逾三歲，擢至總兵，賜號毅勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: After more than three years he was promoted to regional commander and granted the title Yiyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: In a little over three years he rose to regional commander and was awarded the Manchu honorific title Yiyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 既貴，過亳，謁所主，仍易僕廝服，執事上禮益恭，人傳為美談。

translations.literal: Once he had become eminent, passing through Bozhou he called on his former master, again changed into servant's dress, and in performing his duties showed even greater deference — people spread this as a fine story.
translations.idiomatic: After he had risen to high rank, he passed through Bozhou to visit his former patron, deliberately put on servant's clothes again, and waited on him with even greater respect than before — a story people loved to repeat.

sentences.zh: 同治改元，唐訓方撫安徽，裁臨淮軍，而以三營屬慶，毅軍自此始。

translations.literal: At the change of reign title to Tongzhi, Tang Xunfang became governor of Anhui, disbanded the Linhuai Army, and placed three battalions under Song Qing — the Yijun Army began from this.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tongzhi reign began, Tang Xunfang took office as governor of Anhui, cut back the Linhuai Army, and assigned three battalions to Song Qing — the Yijun, or Resolute Army, dates from that moment.

sentences.zh: 三年，苗沛霖圍蒙城，慶絕其餉道。

translations.literal: In the third year Miao Peilin besieged Mengcheng; Song Qing cut off his supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongzhi, Miao Peilin laid siege to Mengcheng, and Song Qing severed his supply lines.

sentences.zh: 會僧格林沁軍至，轟擊之，寇宵遁。

translations.literal: When Senggelinqin's army arrived, they bombarded the rebels and the bandits fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Senggelinqin's forces then arrived, shelled the besiegers, and the rebels slipped away under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 苗酋死，慶為安撫餘眾，自壽州正陽關所蒞皆下。

translations.literal: The Miao chieftain died; Song Qing pacified the remaining followers, and all places from Shouzhou to Zhengyang Pass submitted.
translations.idiomatic: After the Miao leader died, Song Qing pacified the remnant bands, and every post from Shouzhou to Zhengyang Pass came over to the government.

sentences.zh: 兩淮告寧，調赴豫。

translations.literal: When the two Huai regions were reported tranquil, he was transferred to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Once the two Huai circuits were declared at peace, he was ordered to Henan.

sentences.zh: 時張曜為翼長，慶往訪，詳詢地勢寇情。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Yao was deputy commander; Song Qing went to call on him and inquired in detail about the terrain and the rebels' situation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yao was then serving as deputy commander, and Song Qing called on him to ask at length about the lay of the land and the enemy's movements.

sentences.zh: 曜喜曰：「諸將無問及此者，君來，豫之福也！

translations.literal: Zhang Yao said with pleasure: "None of the other generals has asked about this; with your coming, it is Henan's good fortune!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yao said delightedly: No other general has troubled to ask about these things — your arrival is a blessing for Henan!

sentences.zh: 」遂與交驩。

translations.literal: " They thereupon became close friends.
translations.idiomatic: And the two men became fast friends.

sentences.zh: 明年，授南陽鎮總兵。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed regional commander of Nanyang garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed regional commander of the Nanyang garrison.

sentences.zh: 無何，曹州賊勢熾，慶被困鄧州刁河店，會糧罄，勢且不敵。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels' strength at Caozhou flared up; Song Qing was trapped at Diaohedian in Dengzhou; provisions ran out and the situation was untenable.
translations.idiomatic: Before long rebel strength around Caozhou surged, and Song Qing found himself pinned down at Diaohedian in Dengzhou; with food exhausted, he could not long hold out.

sentences.zh: 乃令部將馬玉昆率壯士三百，潛出立營通饋運，軍氣復振，寇乃解去。

translations.literal: He then ordered his subordinate Ma Yukun to lead three hundred picked men to slip out secretly, establish a camp, and open the supply route; army morale revived and the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his lieutenant Ma Yukun with three hundred picked men to steal out by night, raise a camp, and reopen the supply line; spirits rallied, and the besiegers drew off.

sentences.zh: 已而張總愚決河圖北犯，慶據堤迎擊，敗之，西走；

translations.literal: Before long Zhang Zongyu breached the river intending to raid north; Song Qing held the embankment to meet the attack, defeated him, and he fled west;
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhang Zongyu broke the Yellow River dikes planning a northern thrust; Song Qing held the levee line, beat him back, and drove him west;

sentences.zh: 而任柱、賴文光復竄豫，湘軍將劉松山助慶軍盡驅入楚疆，豫略平。

translations.literal: but Ren Zhu and Lai Wenguang again fled into Henan; the Hunan Army general Liu Songshan aided Song Qing's forces in driving them all into Huguang territory, and Henan was largely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: yet Ren Zhu and Lai Wenguang slipped back into Henan until Liu Songshan of the Xiang Army joined Song Qing in driving them into Huguang, after which Henan was largely quiet.

sentences.zh: 巡撫李鶴年因增練兩大軍，令曜領嵩武軍，而以毅軍專屬慶。

translations.literal: Governor Li Henian accordingly enlarged and drilled two great armies, placing Zhang Yao in command of the Songwu Army while the Yijun was placed solely under Song Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Li Henian then expanded two major field forces, putting Zhang Yao in charge of the Songwu Army and leaving the Yijun exclusively under Song Qing.

sentences.zh: 六年，與曜扼黃河，蹙捻至山東，聚而殲之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, together with Zhang Yao he held the Yellow River line, pressed the Nian into Shandong, and destroyed them in a mass engagement.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he and Zhang Yao blocked the Yellow River, cornered the Nian in Shandong, and annihilated them in a final encirclement.

sentences.zh: 論功，賞黃馬褂，更勇號格洪額。

translations.literal: For merit he was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket and his brave-title was changed to Gehong'e.
translations.idiomatic: For these services he received the yellow riding jacket and a new honorific brave-name, Gehong'e.

sentences.zh: 時總愚南擾河津，偪解州，詔慶與曜分守河北。

translations.literal: At that time Zongyu raided south along the Yellow River crossings and pressed Jiezhou; an edict ordered Song Qing and Zhang Yao to divide the defense of the north bank of the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongyu struck south along the ford country and threatened Jiezhou, the court ordered Song Qing and Zhang Yao to split the defense of the north bank.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，捻竄畿疆，慶率師入衛，轉戰雄、任、祁、高間，與諸軍大破之，總愚赴水死。

translations.literal: After a year the Nian raided the capital region; Song Qing led his army to the capital's defense, fought through Xiong, Ren, Qi, and Gao, and with the allied armies inflicted a great defeat; Zongyu drowned himself.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the Nian broke into the metropolitan district; Song Qing marched to the capital's relief, fought through Xiong'an, Renqiu, Qi County, and Gaoyang, and with the allied armies shattered them — Zongyu threw himself into the water and died.

sentences.zh: 予二等輕車都尉，授湖南提督。

translations.literal: He was granted the second-rank Qingche duwei and appointed provincial commander of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was ennobled as second-class Qingche duwei and appointed provincial military commander of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 八年，左宗棠西征，慶引兵從，抵神木，再戰再捷。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Zuo Zongtang marched west on campaign; Song Qing led troops in his train, reached Shenmu, and won repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when Zuo Zongtang marched west, Song Qing took his troops along, reached Shenmu, and won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，命參哈、寧剿匪事，旋移督西川，皆在軍遙領。

translations.literal: The next autumn he was ordered to take part in suppressing bandits in Ha and Ning; soon after he was transferred to govern Sichuan — all while remaining with the army in distant nominal command.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn he was ordered to join operations against bandits in Ha and Ning; he was soon moved to the governorship of Sichuan, but in each case he remained with the field army and held the post only in name.

sentences.zh: 十三年，河、狄撫回閃殿臣叛，楚軍戰失利​​。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Muslim rebel Shan Dianchan in He and Di prefectures rose; the Chu Army suffered defeat in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Muslim rebel Shan Dianchan rose in the He and Di circuit, and the Chu Army was beaten in the field.

sentences.zh: 時慶駐涼州，奉檄往援。

translations.literal: Song Qing was then stationed at Liangzhou and received orders to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qing was then at Liangzhou and received urgent orders to march to their aid.

sentences.zh: 三日馳五百餘裡，抵沙泥站，眾縛其渠以獻，誅之，事遂定。

translations.literal: In three days he rode more than five hundred li, reached Shani Station, the troops bound their chieftain and presented him; he was executed and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: In three days he covered more than five hundred li, reached Shani Station, where his men seized the rebel leader and turned him over; Song Qing had him executed, and the disturbance was ended.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，師還。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu his command marched home.

sentences.zh: 六年，徙防旅順，十餘年，軍容稱盛。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to garrison Lüshun; for more than ten years his army's appearance was acclaimed as outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was posted to Lüshun, where for more than a decade his troops were considered the finest in the garrison.

sentences.zh: 醇賢親王奕枻被命巡閱，嘆為諸軍冠，親解袍服贈之。

translations.literal: Prince Chun Yixuan was ordered to inspect the troops; he sighed that they were foremost among all armies and personally removed his robe and presented it to Song Qing.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chun Yixuan was sent to inspect the forces, he declared Song Qing's unit the best he had seen and took off his own robe to give him.

sentences.zh: 兩宮眷遇優渥，加太子少保、尚書銜。

translations.literal: The two palaces showed him exceptional favor, adding the titles of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowagers heaped honors on him, granting him the brevet ranks of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister.

sentences.zh: 二十年，中日失和，慶統毅軍發於旅順，與諸軍期會東邊九連城。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year China and Japan broke relations; Song Qing led the Yijun Army out from Lüshun to rendezvous with the other armies at Jiuliancheng on the eastern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Guangxu, war broke out with Japan; Song Qing led the Yijun out of Lüshun to join the other columns at Jiuliancheng on the Manchurian frontier.

sentences.zh: 軍未集而平壤已失，廷旨罷總統葉志超，以慶代之。

translations.literal: Before the armies had assembled Pyongyang was already lost; the court ordered the dismissal of supreme commander Ye Zhichao and replaced him with Song Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Before the allied forces could concentrate, Pyongyang had fallen; the court removed supreme commander Ye Zhichao and put Song Qing in his place.

sentences.zh: 慶與諸將行輩相若，驟禀節度，多不懌，以故諸軍七十餘營散無有紀。

translations.literal: Song Qing was of about the same seniority as the other generals; suddenly placed under his command, many were displeased, and for this reason more than seventy battalions of the allied armies were scattered without discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qing was roughly the peers of the other commanders, and many resented suddenly taking orders from him; as a result more than seventy battalions drifted about without unified control.

sentences.zh: 又坐守江北一月，以待日軍過義州，慶頓中路九連城，嚴戒備。

translations.literal: They also sat on the north bank of the river for a month waiting for the Japanese to pass Uiju; Song Qing encamped on the central route at Jiuliancheng with strict precautions.
translations.idiomatic: The allied army also sat idle north of the Yalu for a month, waiting for the Japanese to pass Uiju, while Song Qing held Jiuliancheng on the main road under tight guard.

sentences.zh: 日軍渡鴨綠江，戰失利，直趨鳳凰城，退扼大高嶺。

translations.literal: The Japanese crossed the Yalu; the Chinese were defeated in battle and the enemy drove straight for Fengcheng; they fell back to hold Dagao Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: When the Japanese crossed the Yalu, the Chinese were beaten and the enemy pushed straight for Fengcheng; the allies fell back to hold Dagao Ridge.

sentences.zh: 旅順圍亟，朝命聶士成守之，敕慶往援。

translations.literal: The siege of Lüshun grew urgent; the court ordered Nie Shicheng to defend it and commanded Song Qing to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: As Lüshun came under desperate pressure, the court ordered Nie Shicheng to hold it and directed Song Qing to relieve the port.

sentences.zh: 頓蓋平，屢搗金州不得進，而旅順已失。

translations.literal: He halted at Gaiping, repeatedly struck at Jinzhou but could not advance, and Lüshun had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: He halted at Gaiping and repeatedly probed Jinzhou without making headway — by then Lüshun was already lost.

sentences.zh: 慶退守熊岳，自請治罪，被宥。

translations.literal: Song Qing fell back to defend Xiongyue, asked to be punished, and was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qing withdrew to Xiongyue, asked the court to punish him, and was forgiven.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復州又失。

translations.literal: Before long Fuzhou was also lost.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Fuzhou fell as well.

sentences.zh: 日軍西陷海城，慶亟赴之，擊敵感王寨。

translations.literal: The Japanese seized Haicheng to the west; Song Qing hastened there and attacked the enemy at Ganwangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: When the Japanese took Haicheng in the west, Song Qing rushed to the scene and struck the enemy at Ganwangzhai.

sentences.zh: 前軍方勝，後隊訛傳敵拊背，駭潰，復退守田莊台，遼陽益危。

translations.literal: The vanguard had just won when the rear ranks, on a false report that the enemy was striking from behind, panicked and broke; they again fell back to defend Tianzhuangtai, and Liaoyang grew more precarious.
translations.idiomatic: His vanguard was winning when rumor spread through the rear that the Japanese were attacking from behind; the rear ranks panicked and fled, and the army fell back to Tianzhuangtai while Liaoyang slipped deeper into danger.

sentences.zh: 慶凡五攻城弗能拔，朝廷思倚湘軍，命慶與吳大澂佐劉坤一軍。

translations.literal: Song Qing assaulted the city five times without taking it; the court thought to rely on the Hunan Army and ordered Song Qing and Wu Dacheng to assist Liu Kunyi's forces.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qing assaulted the city five times without success; the court then decided to lean on the Xiang Army and ordered Song Qing and Wu Dacheng to serve under Liu Kunyi.

sentences.zh: 慶率徐邦道、馬玉昆兵萬二千人頓太平山，戰卻之，大澂敗入關。

translations.literal: Song Qing led Xu Bangdao and Ma Yukun with twelve thousand men to encamp at Taiping Mountain, fought and repelled the enemy; Wu Dacheng was defeated and retreated inside the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qing took twelve thousand men under Xu Bangdao and Ma Yukun to Taiping Mountain, beat the Japanese back once, while Wu Dacheng's wing was routed and fled inside Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 慶方以三萬人駐營口，聞警，還扼遼河北岸；

translations.literal: Song Qing had just stationed thirty thousand men at Yingkou; hearing the alarm, he returned to hold the north bank of the Liao;
translations.idiomatic: Song Qing had thirty thousand men at Yingkou; when news of disaster arrived he hurried back to hold the north bank of the Liao;

sentences.zh: 而日軍盡以所獲砲列南岸猛攻，慶軍潰而西，於是遼河以東盡為日有矣。

translations.literal: but the Japanese lined all the captured artillery on the south bank and attacked fiercely; Song Qing's army broke and fled west — thus everything east of the Liao River fell to Japan.
translations.idiomatic: but the Japanese massed every captured gun on the south bank and hammered his line; Song Qing's army broke westward, and everything east of the Liao passed to Japan.

sentences.zh: 詔褫職留任。

translations.literal: An edict stripped him of office but left him at his post.
translations.idiomatic: The court stripped him of rank but kept him in command.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，徙守山海關，入覲，釋處分。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to guard Shanhaiguan; on audience with the throne his punishment was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was posted to Shanhaiguan; when he came to court his penalties were cleared.

sentences.zh: 和議成，留豫軍三十營屬之，賜名武衛左軍，駐錦州。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded, thirty battalions of the Henan Army were left under him, granted the name Left Wuwei Army, and stationed at Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was signed, thirty battalions of the Henan Army were left under him, renamed the Left Wuwei Army, and garrisoned at Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，卒，晉封三等男，予建祠，諡忠勤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died; he was posthumously ennobled as third-class baron, granted a temple, and given the posthumous name Zhongqin.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-eighth year, was posthumously raised to third-class baron, granted a memorial temple, and given the posthumous name Zhongqin (Loyal and Diligent).

sentences.zh: 子天傑，五品京堂，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Tianjie, a fifth-rank official of the capital, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tianjie, a fifth-rank capital official, inherited the peerage.

sentences.zh: 慶從戎久，年幾八十，短衣帕首，躞蹀冰雪中，與士卒同甘苦，人以為難雲。

translations.literal: Song Qing had long been in military service; nearing eighty, in short coat and turban he picked his way through ice and snow, sharing hardship with the soldiers — people considered this hard to match.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qing had been under arms for decades; near eighty he still wore a soldier's short jacket and headcloth, trudging through ice and snow alongside his men — an example people said was hard to equal.

sentences.zh: 呂本元，安徽滁州人。

translations.literal: Lü Benyuan was a native of Chuzhou, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Benyuan came from Chuzhou in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 初隸李鴻章軍，隨剿粵匪、捻匪，轉戰蘇、皖、魯、豫各省。

translations.literal: At first he served under Li Hongzhang's army, following the suppression of Guangdong bandits and Nian rebels, campaigning through Jiangsu, Anhui, Shandong, and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He first served in Li Hongzhang's forces, fighting Taiping and Nian rebels across Jiangsu, Anhui, Shandong, and Henan.

sentences.zh: 援鄂、援陝屢立功，歷保總兵，賞強勇巴圖魯勇號。

translations.literal: In relief of Hubei and Shaanxi he repeatedly won merit, was repeatedly recommended to regional commander, and was granted the brave-title Qiangyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in the Hubei and Shaanxi campaigns, rose through repeated recommendations to regional commander, and received the honorific brave-name Qiangyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 鴻章總督直隸，調入直。

translations.literal: When Hongzhang became governor-general of Zhili, he was transferred into Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hongzhang became governor-general of Zhili, Lü was transferred into that province.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，授四川重慶鎮，仍留統盛軍馬步各營。

translations.literal: Early in Guangxu he was appointed to Chongqing garrison in Sichuan but remained to command the cavalry and infantry battalions of the Sheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangxu reign he was named commander of the Chongqing garrison in Sichuan while continuing to lead the cavalry and infantry of the Sheng Army.

sentences.zh: 中日戰起，檄本元統隊出關，兼程至安州。

translations.literal: When the Sino-Japanese war broke out, an order summoned Benyuan to lead his column out of the Pass; he marched day and night to Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When war with Japan began, he was ordered to lead his column beyond the Pass and reached Anzhou at forced march.

sentences.zh: 平壤失，從宋軍退守大高嶺。

translations.literal: When Pyongyang fell, he followed Song Qing's army in retreat to hold Dagao Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: After Pyongyang fell he withdrew with Song Qing's army to Dagao Ridge.

sentences.zh: 本元令各軍夜樹旗各要隘，廣設疑兵，亙二百餘裡。

translations.literal: Benyuan ordered each army by night to plant flags at every strategic pass and widely set up decoy forces, stretching more than two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Benyuan had each unit plant flags by night at every defile and spread dummy positions along more than two hundred li of front.

sentences.zh: 敵至，疑頓不前，乘其疲襲擊之，復與聶軍敗之分水嶺。

translations.literal: When the enemy arrived they hesitated and did not advance; taking advantage of their fatigue he raided them, and again with Nie's army defeated them at Fenshuiling.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese halted in confusion; he struck them when they were weary, and together with Nie's troops beat them again at Fenshuiling.

sentences.zh: 議成，還直。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded he returned to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: After the peace settlement he returned to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，拳禍起，署天津鎮，擢直隸提督，統淮、練各軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer disaster arose; he acted as commander of Tianjin garrison, was promoted to provincial commander of Zhili, and commanded the Huai and militia armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, when the Boxer crisis erupted, he acted as Tianjin garrison commander, was promoted to provincial commander of Zhili, and took charge of Huai and militia units.

sentences.zh: 剿匪受彈傷，事平，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In suppressing bandits he received a gunshot wound; when the affair was settled he was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: He was wounded by gunfire while hunting bandits; when order was restored he received the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 調浙江，勤訓練，尤嚴治盜，常親督隊入山搜剿，連斃匪首。

translations.literal: Transferred to Zhejiang, he drilled diligently and was especially strict in suppressing bandits, often personally leading troops into the mountains to search and destroy, repeatedly killing bandit chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Zhejiang, he drilled his men relentlessly and was especially hard on bandits, often leading search parties into the hills himself and killing several chieftains in succession.

sentences.zh: 浙省議裁綠營，本元贊畫始就緒。

translations.literal: When Zhejiang deliberated cutting the Green Standard Army, Benyuan planned the undertaking until it was brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhejiang debated cutting the Green Standard garrisons, Benyuan drew up the plans that finally carried the reform through.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年，病，乞罷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuantong he fell ill and asked to resign.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuantong he fell ill and asked to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 徐邦道，四川涪州人。

translations.literal: Xu Bangdao was a native of Fuzhou, Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Bangdao came from Fuzhou in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 初從楚軍討粵寇，積勳至參將。

translations.literal: At first he followed the Chu Army in campaigning against the Guangdong rebels, accumulating merit until he reached the rank of deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first campaigned with the Chu Army against the Taiping rebels and rose on merit to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 還本籍籌防，解城圍，遷副將。

translations.literal: Returning to his native place to organize defense, he lifted a siege and was transferred to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: Back home organizing local defense, he raised a siege and was promoted to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 越境援陝西漢中，賜號冠勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Crossing the border he aided Hanzhong in Shaanxi and was granted the title Guanyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing into Shaanxi he reinforced Hanzhong and received the honorific title Guanyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 旋坐漢中失守，褫職。

translations.literal: Soon after, because Hanzhong was lost, he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon stripped of rank when Hanzhong fell on his watch.

sentences.zh: 嗣從副將楊鼎勳援蘇，再援浙、閩，以戰功釋處分。

translations.literal: Later he followed Vice Commander Yang Dingxun in relief of Jiangsu, then again aided Zhejiang and Fujian, and through battle merit his punishment was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: He then served under Vice Commander Yang Dingxun in Jiangsu, later in Zhejiang and Fujian, and won back his rank through battlefield service.

sentences.zh: 同治六年，從劉銘傳剿平東捻，复官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tongzhi he followed Liu Mingchuan in wiping out the eastern Nian and was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tongzhi he served under Liu Mingchuan in destroying the eastern Nian and was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 明年，張總愚犯減河，邦道嚴扼橋口，大敗之。

translations.literal: The next year Zhang Zongyu attacked along the Jian River; Bangdao strictly held the bridgehead and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Zhang Zongyu struck along the Jian River, Bangdao held the bridgehead firmly and routed him.

sentences.zh: 更勇號鏗僧額，遷總兵，署江蘇徐州鎮。

translations.literal: His brave-title was changed to Kengseng'e; he was promoted to regional commander and acted as commander of Xuzhou garrison in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: His honorific brave-name was changed to Kengseng'e, he was promoted to regional commander, and acted as commander of the Xuzhou garrison in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，擢提督，調駐天津軍糧城，授正定鎮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he was promoted to provincial commander, transferred to garrison at Junliangcheng near Tianjin, and appointed to Zhengding garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Guangxu he was made provincial commander, posted to Junliangcheng near Tianjin, and appointed to the Zhengding garrison.

sentences.zh: 東事起，慶以旅順守將赴防九連城，李鴻章別令薑桂題等守旅順，邦道助之。

translations.literal: When the eastern crisis arose, Song Qing as Lüshun garrison commander went to defend Jiuliancheng; Li Hongzhang separately ordered Jiang Guiti and others to defend Lüshun, and Bangdao assisted them.
translations.idiomatic: When war in the east began, Song Qing left his Lüshun post for Jiuliancheng while Li Hongzhang ordered Jiang Guiti and others to hold Lüshun — Bangdao served under them.

sentences.zh: 日軍入貔子窩，邦道語諸將曰：「金州若失，則旅順不可守，請分兵御之。

translations.literal: When the Japanese entered Biziwowa, Bangdao said to the generals: "If Jinzhou is lost, Lüshun cannot be held — please divide forces to defend it."
translations.idiomatic: When the Japanese landed at Biziwowa, Bangdao told the other commanders: If we lose Jinzhou, Lüshun cannot be held — send troops to block them there.

sentences.zh: 」諸將各不相統，莫之應。

translations.literal: " The generals were not under unified command and none responded.
translations.idiomatic: None answered: each commander answered only to himself.

sentences.zh: 邦道自率所部趨大連灣。

translations.literal: Bangdao himself led his unit toward Dalian Bay.
translations.idiomatic: Bangdao marched his own brigade toward Dalian Bay alone.

sentences.zh: 是時銘軍分統趙懷益守其地，邦道至，固請兵，乃分步旅隨邦道行。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao Huaiyi of the Ming Army's detached command garrisoned the place; when Bangdao arrived he firmly requested troops, and infantry were then detached to follow Bangdao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huaiyi of the Ming Army held the bay; when Bangdao arrived he pressed for reinforcements, and a detachment of infantry was finally sent with him.

sentences.zh: 日軍大集，遂佔金州，進偪大連，懷益奔旅順。

translations.literal: The Japanese gathered in force, then seized Jinzhou and advanced to threaten Dalian; Huaiyi fled to Lüshun.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese concentrated in strength, took Jinzhou, and pressed Dalian; Huaiyi fled to Lüshun.

sentences.zh: 越十日，日軍來爭旅順，諸將相顧無措，邦道率殘卒至，憤甚，思自效，請增兵，不許；

translations.literal: After ten days the Japanese came to contest Lüshun; the generals looked at one another helplessly; Bangdao arrived with his remnant troops, was deeply angered and wished to redeem himself, requested reinforcements but was refused;
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later the Japanese moved on Lüshun; the commanders stood paralyzed until Bangdao arrived with his battered remnant, burning to redeem himself; he asked for more men and was refused;

sentences.zh: 請械，許之，乃率眾拒戰土城子，挫之。

translations.literal: he requested arms and was permitted; he then led his men to resist at Tuchengzi and repulsed the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: he asked for arms and got them, then led his men to Tuchengzi and threw the Japanese back once.

sentences.zh: 日軍大至，乃退。

translations.literal: When the Japanese came in force he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the main Japanese force arrived he fell back.

sentences.zh: 道員龔照嶼先一日遁，諸將亦奪民船以濟，蓋日軍未至而旅順已墟矣。

translations.literal: Circuit Intendant Gong Zhaoyu had fled the day before; the generals also seized civilian boats to cross — in effect Lüshun was already in ruins before the Japanese arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit Intendant Gong Zhaoyu had fled the day before; the generals seized civilian boats to escape — Lüshun was already a ghost town before the Japanese entered.

sentences.zh: 邦道奔復州依慶，詔褫職。

translations.literal: Bangdao fled to Fuzhou and placed himself under Song Qing; an edict stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Bangdao fled to Fuzhou and joined Song Qing; the court stripped him of rank.

sentences.zh: 慶令守蓋州，邦道自牛莊移師還，而蓋平亦已失，合章高元擊之，弗勝。

translations.literal: Song Qing ordered him to defend Gaizhou; Bangdao moved his army back from Niuzhuang, but Gaiping had also fallen; joining Zhang Gaoyuan he attacked but could not win.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qing ordered him to hold Gaizhou; Bangdao marched back from Niuzhuang, but Gaiping had already fallen; he and Zhang Gaoyuan attacked together and were beaten.

sentences.zh: 桂題往援，邦道請夜搗蓋平，桂題辭，諸軍皆退營口。

translations.literal: Jiang Guiti went to the rescue; Bangdao requested a night assault on Gaiping; Jiang Guiti declined, and all armies fell back to Yingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Guiti came to help; Bangdao proposed a night raid on Gaiping, but Jiang refused and the whole allied force withdrew to Yingkou.

sentences.zh: 邦道乃從慶擊敵太平山，與玉昆力戰卻之，俄仍敗潰。

translations.literal: Bangdao then followed Song Qing in attacking the enemy at Taiping Mountain; with Yukun he fought fiercely and repelled them, but soon they were again defeated and routed.
translations.idiomatic: Bangdao then fought with Song Qing at Taiping Mountain; he and Yukun drove the Japanese back once, but the line soon collapsed again.

sentences.zh: 復與湘軍將李光久攻海城，亦弗克，遂退。

translations.literal: Again with the Hunan Army general Li Guangjiu he attacked Haicheng but also could not take it, and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Xiang Army general Li Guangjiu in another assault on Haicheng, failed again, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，卒，复官，予優恤。

translations.literal: After a year he died; his office was restored and favorable condolence grants were given.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died; his rank was posthumously restored and his family granted generous relief.

sentences.zh: 馬玉昆，字景山，安徽蒙城人。

translations.literal: Ma Yukun, styled Jingshan, was a man of Mengcheng in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yukun, whose style was Jingshan, came from Mengcheng in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 以武童從宋慶攻捻，積功至都司，賜號振勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: As a military student he followed Song Qing against the Nian, accumulated merit to colonel, and was granted the title Zhenyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a military student under Song Qing in campaigns against the Nian rebels, rose through merit to colonel, and received the Manchu honorific Zhenyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 任柱等困慶登州，玉昆銳身馳救，圍立解，繇是以驍果名。

translations.literal: Ren Zhu and others trapped Song at Dengzhou; Yukun rushed himself to the rescue, the siege was immediately lifted, and from this he gained a name for valor.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren Zhu and other Nian leaders had Song Qing trapped at Dengzhou, Yukun dashed to the rescue in person; the siege lifted at once, and from that day his reputation for fierce courage spread.

sentences.zh: 捻平，擢總兵。

translations.literal: When the Nian were pacified, he was promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: After the Nian rebellion was suppressed, he was promoted to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 剿秦、隴回，數獲勝，更勇號曰博奇。

translations.literal: He suppressed the Muslims of Qin and Long, won victories repeatedly, and his brave title was changed to Boji.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Muslim rebels in Qin and Long, he won battle after battle; his martial honorific was then changed to Boji.

sentences.zh: 既克肅州，賜頭品服。

translations.literal: After Suzhou was taken, he was granted first-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Once Suzhou fell, he was awarded first-rank court dress.

sentences.zh: 嗣從金順出嘉峪關，連下烏魯木齊、昌吉、瑪納斯，擒其渠黑瞎子。

translations.literal: Thereafter he followed Jin Shun through Jiayuguan, took in succession Urumqi, Changji, and Manas, and captured their chieftain Heixiazi.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched with Jin Shun beyond Jiayuguan, capturing Urumqi, Changji, and Manas in succession and taking the rebel leader known as Heixiazi.

sentences.zh: 天山南北告寧，賞黃馬褂，予世職。

translations.literal: North and south of the Tianshan reported tranquility; he was rewarded with a yellow jacket and granted a hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was declared on both sides of the Tianshan, he received the yellow jacket and a hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 玉昆居西域先後十餘年，收復名城以十數，暇輒使部下屯墾闢地利。

translations.literal: Yukun dwelt in the Western Regions for more than ten years in all, recovered famous cities by the tens, and in spare time always had his subordinates farm garrison fields to open the land's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Yukun spent more than a decade in the far west altogether, recovering a dozen major cities; whenever campaigning slackened he set his men to garrison farming to develop the frontier.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章疏薦將才，謂可繼宋慶。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang memorialized recommending him as a commander of talent, saying he could succeed Song Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang memorialized him as a commander of rare ability, declaring that he could carry on where Song Qing left off.

sentences.zh: 光緒間，調赴直隸。

translations.literal: During the Guangxu reign he was transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangxu era he was transferred to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 二十年，補授山西太原鎮。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed in full capacity as garrison commander of Taiyuan in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Guangxu he received appointment as garrison commander of Taiyuan, Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 會日朝構釁，玉昆統毅軍赴援，次平壤，壁南門外大同江。

translations.literal: When Japan and Korea came to hostilities, Yukun commanded the Yijun to go to their aid, halted at Pyongyang, and encamped south of the outer gate on the Datong River.
translations.idiomatic: War broke out between Japan and Korea; Yukun led the Resolute Army to Korea, encamped at Pyongyang, and fortified the south gate along the Datong River.

sentences.zh: 日軍來攻，玉昆守東岸，血戰久，援至，敵敗去。

translations.literal: Japanese troops came to attack; Yukun held the east bank, fought a bloody battle for a long time, reinforcements arrived, and the enemy was defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Japanese attacked, Yukun held the east bank in a prolonged bloody fight until reinforcements arrived and the enemy fell back.

sentences.zh: 已而玄武門失，葉志超令其速撤軍，乃歸平壤。

translations.literal: Before long Xuanwu Gate was lost; Ye Zhichao ordered him to withdraw the army swiftly, and he then returned to Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xuanwu Gate fell; Ye Zhichao ordered a rapid withdrawal, and Yukun pulled back into Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 日軍佔蓋平，諸將皆退營口。

translations.literal: The Japanese occupied Gaiping, and the generals all retreated to Yingkou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Japanese took Gaiping, the commanders fell back to Yingkou.

sentences.zh: 玉昆從慶頓太平山，日軍猛攻之，玉昆戰最力，擊退其眾。

translations.literal: Yukun followed Qing and halted at Taiping Mountain; the Japanese attacked it fiercely, Yukun fought with the greatest effort, and repelled their force.
translations.idiomatic: Yukun joined Song Qing at Taiping Mountain; when the Japanese assaulted in strength, Yukun fought hardest of all and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 無何，日軍大集，慶陷重圍，墜馬負創，玉昆抉圍入，翼之出，傷亡殊多。

translations.literal: Before long the Japanese massed in great numbers; Qing fell into heavy encirclement, fell from his horse wounded, Yukun broke through the encirclement to enter, escorted him out on both sides, and casualties were exceptionally heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Japanese forces concentrated; Song Qing was surrounded, thrown from his horse and wounded. Yukun cut his way in, shielded him out, and the losses on both sides were severe.

sentences.zh: 轉戰田莊台、感王寨，以千餘人抗強敵，屹然自全。

translations.literal: He fought successively at Tianzhuangtai and Ganwangzhai; with a little more than a thousand men he resisted a strong enemy and stood firm, preserving himself intact.
translations.idiomatic: He fought on at Tianzhuangtai and Ganwangzhai, holding off superior forces with barely a thousand men and emerging intact.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，擢浙江提督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to provincial military commander of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Guangxu he was made provincial commander of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 明年，調還直隸。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred back to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred back to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 適拳匪肇亂，聯軍入寇，玉昆統武衛左軍御之。

translations.literal: Just then the Boxers rose in rebellion and the allied armies invaded; Yukun commanded the Left Wuwei Army to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: The Boxer uprising broke out just then, and allied armies invaded; Yukun took command of the Left Wuwei Army to meet them.

sentences.zh: 初戰天津，繼戰北倉，相持月餘，卒以無援退。

translations.literal: He first fought at Tianjin, then fought at Beicang, stalemate lasted more than a month, and in the end, having no relief, he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He fought first at Tianjin, then at Beicang; the standoff lasted over a month, but with no reinforcements he was forced to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 車駕西幸，命隨扈。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage went west on tour; he was ordered to follow in escort.
translations.idiomatic: When the court fled west, he was ordered to join the escort.

sentences.zh: 又明年，還京，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Again the next year he returned to the capital and was given Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he returned to the capital and was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，朝陽土寇竊發，玉昆倍道應赴，破其卡，生擒首惡鄧萊峰誅之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year bandits of Chaoyang rose in secret; Yukun hurried by double marches to answer the call, broke their stockade, captured alive the chief villain Deng Laifeng and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year local bandits raided Chaoyang; Yukun marched at forced pace, stormed their fort, captured the ringleader Deng Laifeng alive, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，病卒，贈太子太保，予二等輕車都尉，諡忠武。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he died of illness; he was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted second-class Qingche duwei, and given the posthumous name Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he died of illness; the court posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted second-class Qingche duwei, and honored him with the posthumous name Zhongwu, Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 依克唐阿，字堯山，扎拉里氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人，吉林駐防。

translations.literal: I Ketang'a, styled Yaoshan, of the Zhalar clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner, garrisoned at Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: I Ketang'a, whose style was Yaoshan, belonged to the Zhalar clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner stationed at Jilin.

sentences.zh: 以馬甲從征江南。

translations.literal: As an armored soldier he followed the campaign in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He first saw service as an armored cavalryman in the Jiangnan campaigns.

sentences.zh: 移師討捻，敗張洛行於大回村、濉溪口，屢著戰績，積勳至佐領。

translations.literal: His army was shifted to suppress the Nian; he defeated Zhang Luoxing at Dahui Village and the Suixi ford, repeatedly distinguished himself in battle, and accumulated merit to company commander rank.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to operations against the Nian, he defeated Zhang Luoxing at Dahui Village and Suixi Ford, won repeated victories, and rose to company commander.

sentences.zh: 同治初，馬賊陷伊通，依克唐阿以少襲眾，斬其酋劉果發等，又破之昌圖，攻克劉家店，复長春廳，遷協領，賜號法什尚阿巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Early in Tongzhi, horse bandits took Yitong; I Ketang'a with few struck many, beheaded their chieftain Liu Guofa and others, again defeated them at Changtu, captured Liujiadian, recovered Changchun subprefecture, was moved to vice commandant, and was granted the title Fashishang'a Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi reign, mounted bandits seized Yitong; I Ketang'a attacked with inferior numbers, killed their leader Liu Guofa and others, routed them again at Changtu, took Liujiadian, recovered Changchun, was promoted to vice commandant, and received the title Fashishang'a Batulu.

sentences.zh: 搜捕殘匪，獲白凌阿、焦西平，晉副都統。

translations.literal: Hunting down remnant bandits, he captured Bai Ling'a and Jiao Xiping and was advanced to vice commandant of the banner.
translations.idiomatic: In mop-up operations he captured Bai Ling'a and Jiao Xiping and was promoted to banner vice commandant.

sentences.zh: 十一年，補官黑龍江。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he filled a post in Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he received a regular appointment in Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年，移呼蘭，呼蘭設副都統自此始。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu he was moved to Hulan; the establishment of a vice commandant at Hulan began from this.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu year five he was transferred to Hulan, where the post of vice commandant was created for the first time.

sentences.zh: 明年，母憂歸。

translations.literal: The next year, on his mother's mourning, he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he went home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 時俄人以議改伊犁條約有違言，烏里雅蘇台參贊喜昌夙諗依克唐阿諳戰術，請敕就近募獵戶守琿春。

translations.literal: At that time the Russians, because of disputes over revising the Ili treaty, had words of breach; the Uliastai consultant Xichang had long known I Ketang'a was versed in tactics and requested an edict to recruit hunters nearby to guard Hunchun.
translations.idiomatic: Russia was raising objections to revisions of the Ili treaty; the Uliastai consultant Xichang, who had long known I Ketang'a's mastery of tactics, asked the throne to authorize recruiting local hunters to defend Hunchun.

sentences.zh: 會吉林戒嚴，依克唐阿遂募兵五千擇隘分守，而自率師駐其地。

translations.literal: When Jilin was placed on alert, I Ketang'a then recruited five thousand troops, chose passes to divide and guard, and himself led the army to garrison that place.
translations.idiomatic: Jilin went on alert; I Ketang'a raised five thousand men, posted them at strategic passes, and personally led the main force to the sector.

sentences.zh: 琿春故重鎮，其東南海參崴，俄尤數窺伺，廷議設副都統鎮之，於是又改調琿春。

translations.literal: Hunchun was formerly a key stronghold; to its southeast was Vladivostok, and Russia especially often watched and coveted it; court deliberation set a vice commandant to guard it, and so he was again transferred to Hunchun.
translations.idiomatic: Hunchun was a strategic town facing Vladivostok to the southeast, which Russia watched with particular greed; the court decided to station a vice commandant there, and I Ketang'a was transferred accordingly.

sentences.zh: 十年，被命佐吉林軍事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was ordered to assist Jilin military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was ordered to assist in Jilin military affairs.

sentences.zh: 十五年，擢黑龍江將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to general of Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was made general of Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 二十年，日朝戰起，依克唐阿請率軍自效，乃進咸鏡道，繞赴漢城迎擊，上嘉之。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year war between Japan and Korea arose; I Ketang'a requested to lead an army to offer his service, advanced along the Hamgyong circuit, went around to Seoul to meet and strike the enemy, and the emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out between Japan and Korea in the twentieth year, I Ketang'a volunteered for active command, advanced by the Hamgyong route, and swung toward Seoul to intercept the enemy; the throne commended him.

sentences.zh: 左寶貴軍失利平壤，日軍西進，命移駐九連城。

translations.literal: Zuo Baogui's army was defeated at Pyongyang; the Japanese advanced west; he was ordered to move his garrison to Jiuliancheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Zuo Baogui's defeat at Pyongyang and the Japanese push westward, he was ordered to Jiuliancheng.

sentences.zh: 尋以日軍渡江來攻，復令徙上游御之。

translations.literal: Soon, because Japanese troops crossed the river to attack, he was again ordered to move upstream to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Japanese crossed the river to attack, he was ordered farther upstream to block them.

sentences.zh: 依克唐阿與戰於蒲石河，連克蒲石河口、古樓子。

translations.literal: I Ketang'a fought them at Pushi River and in succession took Pushihekou and Gulouzi.
translations.idiomatic: I Ketang'a fought at the Pushi River and in succession captured Pushihekou and Gulouzi.

sentences.zh: 宋慶退駐大高嶺，依克唐阿孤軍不能獨守，遂退寬甸。

translations.literal: Song Qing withdrew and garrisoned Dagao Ridge; I Ketang'a's isolated army could not hold alone, and he then withdrew to Kuandian.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qing fell back to Dagao Ridge; left alone, I Ketang'a could not hold his position and withdrew to Kuandian.

sentences.zh: 宋軍南援旅、大，聶士成軍接防，乃定夾攻之約。

translations.literal: Song's army went south to aid Lüshun and Dalian; Nie Shicheng's army took over defense; then they fixed a plan for a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qing marched south to relieve Port Arthur and Dalian while Nie Shicheng's force took over the line; the two commanders then agreed on a joint enveloping attack.

sentences.zh: 依軍由寬甸繞進賽馬集迎擊日軍，先戰懸羊砬子，連勝之草嶺河、通遠堡、草河口。

translations.literal: I's army from Kuandian went around to advance on Saimaji to meet and strike the Japanese; they first fought at Xianyanglazi and in succession were victorious at Caolinghe, Tongyuanbao, and Caohekou.
translations.idiomatic: I Ketang'a swung from Kuandian toward Saimaji to intercept the Japanese, winning first at Xianyanglazi and then in succession at Caolinghe, Tongyuanbao, and Caohekou.

sentences.zh: 日軍大集，橫斷聶、依兩軍，士成亟趨分水嶺拊其背，依軍還擊之，陣斬一中尉。

translations.literal: The Japanese massed in great numbers and cut across horizontally between Nie's and I's two armies; Shicheng urgently hastened to Fenshuiling to strike their rear; I's army turned back to strike them and slew one lieutenant in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese concentrated in force and severed Nie and I Ketang'a from each other; Nie Shicheng rushed to Fenshuiling to hit their rear while I Ketang'a counterattacked and killed a Japanese lieutenant in the field.

sentences.zh: 又西而東，大戰於金家河，軍稍挫。

translations.literal: Again west then east, they fought a great battle at Jinjiahe and the army was slightly set back.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting westward and then east again, they met in a major battle at Jinjiahe, where his force suffered a slight reverse.

sentences.zh: 日軍先已佔鳳凰城，依克唐阿謀襲之，分左右翼以進，戰一面山，敵來爭，左翼潰，右翼統領永山遇伏死，依克唐阿保餘軍退，詔革職圖後效。

translations.literal: The Japanese had already occupied Fengcheng beforehand; I Ketang'a planned to assault it, divided into left and right wings to advance, fought at Yimianshan, the enemy came to contest it, the left wing collapsed, the right-wing commander Yongshan met an ambush and died, I Ketang'a preserved the remnant army and withdrew, and an edict stripped his office pending later merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese already held Fengcheng; I Ketang'a planned an assault with two wings, fought at Yimianshan, saw his left wing routed and his right-wing commander Yongshan killed in an ambush, saved what troops he could and withdrew, and was stripped of rank pending future service.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，海城陷，遼西危棘，詔責長順守遼陽，依克唐阿助之，發帑金五十萬濟依軍。

translations.literal: After a year Haicheng fell, western Liaodong was perilously thorny, an edict charged Zhang Shun to defend Liaoyang, I Ketang'a assisted him, and five hundred thousand taels from the treasury were issued to aid I's army.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Haicheng fell and western Liaodong faced disaster; the court ordered Zhang Shun to hold Liaoyang with I Ketang'a's assistance and allocated five hundred thousand taels from the treasury to his army.

sentences.zh: 既至，議以攻為守。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, they deliberated to use attack as defense.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival they resolved to take the offensive as their best defense.

sentences.zh: 乃集諸將置酒，取刀刺臂血，攪而飲之，相矢以死。

translations.literal: Then they gathered the generals, set out wine, took a knife and stabbed the arm for blood, stirred it and drank, and pledged one another unto death.
translations.idiomatic: He assembled his officers for a feast, cut his arm with a knife, mixed the blood into the wine, and they drank together, swearing to stand or fall as one.

sentences.zh: 依軍遂進取海城，軍騰鰲堡、耿莊，數戰弗勝。

translations.literal: I's army then advanced to take Haicheng, the army at Teng'aobao and Gengzhuang, fought several times without victory.
translations.idiomatic: I Ketang'a's force then pushed toward Haicheng by way of Teng'aobao and Gengzhuang, but several assaults failed.

sentences.zh: 會榮和至軍，亟趣之出。

translations.literal: When Rong He arrived at the army, he urgently urged them to go out.
translations.idiomatic: Rong He then joined the army and urgently pressed for an offensive.

sentences.zh: 榮和先進北路，奪三卡，其左樹木幽深，令隱兵備抄襲，而自列陣曠野，伏槍以待。

translations.literal: Rong He first advanced on the northern route and seized three forts; on his left the trees were deep and secluded; he ordered hidden troops prepared for flanking raids, while he himself drew up battle lines on open ground and lay in wait with muskets ambushed.
translations.idiomatic: Rong He led the northern column, took three fortified posts, hid troops in the dense woods on his left for a flanking strike, and himself drew up in the open with musketeers lying in wait.

sentences.zh: 日軍據山巔轟擊我師，彈落積雪中，漬不發。

translations.literal: Japanese troops held the mountain crest and bombarded our army; shells fell in accumulated snow and, soaked through, failed to fire.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese gunners on the heights shelled his line, but shells landing in deep snow soaked through and failed to explode.

sentences.zh: 我師還擊，僕者眾，再發再僕。

translations.literal: Our army struck back; those who fell were many, and again they rose and again they fell.
translations.idiomatic: His men counterattacked; the enemy fell in waves, rose again, and fell again.

sentences.zh: 眾爭傍山出，伏槍具舉，死以百數。

translations.literal: The masses strove to come out along the mountain; ambushed muskets all fired together, and the dead numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: As the Japanese tried to work along the slopes, every ambush musket fired at once and hundreds were killed.

sentences.zh: 榮和所部募自塞邊外，善避擊，傷者恆少，所謂「東山獵戶」也。

translations.literal: Rong He's command was recruited from beyond the frontier of the pass; they were skilled at avoiding strikes, and the wounded were always few — the so-called Eastern Mountain hunters.
translations.idiomatic: Rong He's troops were frontier hunters from beyond the pass, adept at evading fire; casualties were always light — the men known as the Eastern Mountain hunters.

sentences.zh: 是役以千人抗日軍數千，故依軍聲譽遠出諸軍上。

translations.literal: In this battle a thousand men resisted Japanese troops by the thousands, and therefore I's army's reputation far exceeded the other armies.
translations.idiomatic: In this fight a thousand men held off several thousand Japanese, and I Ketang'a's reputation rose far above that of the other forces.

sentences.zh: 罷戰詔下，日人將歸我遼東，依克唐阿力請三路分兵鎮懾，稱旨。

translations.literal: When the edict to cease fighting was issued, the Japanese were about to return our Liaodong; I Ketang'a strongly requested three routes to divide troops for garrison and deterrence, and it accorded with the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceasefire was proclaimed and Japan prepared to return Liaodong, I Ketang'a strongly urged a three-route garrison to hold the territory; the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 又條上練兵隊、築砲台、造鐵路、制槍械、開礦產、治團練六事，朝旨以礦政尤要，敕妥籌開採。

translations.literal: He also itemized and submitted six matters — training companies, building batteries, constructing railways, manufacturing firearms, opening mineral resources, and organizing militia — and the court's directive held mining policy especially important and ordered proper planning for extraction.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted six proposals: drill corps, fortifications, railways, firearms manufacture, mining, and local militia; the court singled out mining as especially urgent and ordered careful development.

sentences.zh: 又明年，晉頭品秩，授鑲黃旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: Again the next year he was advanced to first-rank grade and appointed commandant of the Bordered Yellow Chinese Banner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to first rank and made commandant of the Bordered Yellow Chinese Banner.

sentences.zh: 其秋，出為盛京將軍。

translations.literal: That autumn he went out as general of Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was appointed general of Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 既蒞事，糾貪墨，整營製，晰分釐稅，歲增餉銀數十萬。

translations.literal: Once he assumed affairs, he corrected corruption, put camp regulations in order, clearly divided lijin taxes, and each year increased pay silver by several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he rooted out corruption, tightened army discipline, clarified tax assessments, and increased annual revenue by hundreds of thousands of taels.

sentences.zh: 复撤還金州奉軍，杜俄人藉口，境內稱治。

translations.literal: He again withdrew and recalled the Feng army at Jinzhou, blocked Russians' pretexts, and within the territory it was called well governed.
translations.idiomatic: He also withdrew the Feng garrison from Jinzhou, denying Russia a pretext for interference, and the region was said to be at peace.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒，諡誠勇，予建祠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died; his posthumous name was Chengyong, and a temple was granted to be built.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he died; he was given the posthumous name Chengyong, Loyal and Brave, and a memorial temple.

sentences.zh: 依克唐阿勇而有謀，性仁厚，不嗜殺，每有俘獲，不妄戮一人。

translations.literal: I Ketang'a was brave and possessed stratagem, his nature humane and generous, not addicted to killing; whenever there were captives taken, he did not recklessly execute a single person.
translations.idiomatic: I Ketang'a was courageous and resourceful, humane by nature and no lover of bloodshed; he never put captives to death without cause.

sentences.zh: 轉戰吳、皖、魯、豫，先後救出難民以十數万計，至今人屍祝之。

translations.literal: Fighting successively in Wu, Wan, Lu, and Yu, he in all rescued refugees by the hundreds of thousands; to this day people offer him sacrifice and prayer.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning across Jiangsu, Anhui, Shandong, and Henan, he saved refugees by the hundreds of thousands; people still offer him sacrifice in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 初與長順訂兄弟交，長順兄事之。

translations.literal: At first he and Zhang Shun made a pact of brotherhood; Zhang Shun treated him with the ceremony due an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhang Shun had sworn brotherhood; Zhang Shun treated him as the elder of the two.

sentences.zh: 及議遼陽戰守，語不協。

translations.literal: When they deliberated on fighting or holding at Liaoyang, their words did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When they debated strategy at Liaoyang, they could not agree.

sentences.zh: 依克唐阿毅然獨任其難，曰：「孰使我為兄也者？

translations.literal: I Ketang'a resolutely undertook the hardship alone and said: Who made me the elder brother?
translations.idiomatic: I Ketang'a resolutely took on the hardest task alone, saying: Who was it that made me the elder brother?

sentences.zh: 」其雅量如此。

translations.literal: Such was his magnanimous measure.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the breadth of his character.

sentences.zh: 榮和，字育堂。

translations.literal: Rong He, styled Yutang.
translations.idiomatic: Rong He, whose style was Yutang.

sentences.zh: 二等侍衛，官至副都統。

translations.literal: Second-class imperial bodyguard; his official career reached vice commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from second-class imperial bodyguard to vice commandant.

sentences.zh: 戰後所部育字營多驕縱，命李秉衡查辦，革職治罪。

translations.literal: After the war his command, the Yu-character battalion, was largely arrogant and unbridled; he was ordered investigated by Li Bingheng, stripped of office and punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: After the war his Yu Battalion grew insubordinate; Li Bingheng was ordered to investigate, and Rong He was stripped of rank and punished.

sentences.zh: 長順，字鶴汀，達呼裡郭貝爾氏，隸滿洲正白旗，世居布特哈。

translations.literal: Zhang Shun, styled Heting, of the Daohuri Gorbier clan, attached to the Manchu Plain White Banner, his family dwelling for generations at Buteha.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shun, whose style was Heting, belonged to the Daohuri Gorbier clan of the Plain White Banner, with his family long settled at Buteha.

sentences.zh: 起家藍翎侍衛，隨文宗車駕狩熱河。

translations.literal: He began his career as a blue-lance bodyguard and followed the Wenzong emperor's carriage on the hunt at Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a blue-lance bodyguard and accompanied the Xianfeng emperor on the imperial hunt at Rehe.

sentences.zh: 會馬賊陷朝陽，從大學士文祥討平之。

translations.literal: When horse bandits took Chaoyang, he followed Grand Secretary Wen Xiang to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When mounted bandits seized Chaoyang, he campaigned under Grand Secretary Wen Xiang and helped suppress them.

sentences.zh: 嗣復從侍郎勝保徵捻，轉戰直、魯、皖、豫，以驍勇稱。

translations.literal: Thereafter he again followed Vice Minister Sheng Bao to campaign against the Nian, fought successively in Zhi, Lu, Wan, and Yu, and was known for fierce valor.
translations.idiomatic: He then served under Vice Minister Sheng Bao against the Nian, fighting across Zhili, Shandong, Anhui, and Henan, and won fame for reckless courage.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，解潁州圍，以功遷二等。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he relieved the siege of Yingzhou and, for merit, was moved to second class.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he lifted the siege of Yingzhou and was promoted to second rank for his service.

sentences.zh: 多隆阿主陝西軍事，調赴軍，至潼關，大敗寇眾，賜號恩特赫恩巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Duo Long'a presided over Shaanxi military affairs; he was transferred to the army, reached Tongguan, inflicted a great defeat on the bandit masses, and was granted the title Entehe'en Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: When Duo Long'a commanded in Shaanxi, Zhang Shun was transferred to his force, won a great victory at Tongguan, and received the title Entehe'en Batulu.

sentences.zh: 進攻咸陽馬家堡，被巨創，援至，又大破之，咸陽复，晉頭等。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Majiabao at Xianyang, he received a grave wound; relief arrived and he again inflicted a great defeat; Xianyang was recovered and he was advanced to first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking Majiabao near Xianyang he was badly wounded, but reinforcements arrived, he routed the enemy again, recovered Xianyang, and was promoted to first rank.

sentences.zh: 三年，悍回馬化隆據寧夏，分其黨駐清水堡成犄角，師久攻不下。

translations.literal: In the third year the fierce Muslim Ma Hualong held Ningxia, divided his partisans to garrison Qingshuibao forming horned pincers, and the army long attacked without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the rebel Ma Hualong held Ningxia, posted detachments at Qingshuibao in a pincer defense, and the siege dragged on without success.

sentences.zh: 長順曰：「不先翦其羽翼，城未可克也！

translations.literal: Zhang Shun said: If we do not first cut his wings and feathers, the city cannot be taken!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shun said: Unless we cut off his outlying wings first, we will never take the city!

sentences.zh: 」乃自靈州襲清水堡，乘勝取寧夏，拔之，晉副都統，賜頭品服。

translations.literal: Then from Lingzhou he raided Qingshuibao, followed victory to take Ningxia, stormed and took it, was advanced to vice commandant, and was granted first-rank dress.
translations.idiomatic: He then struck Qingshuibao from Lingzhou, swept on to capture Ningxia, was promoted to vice commandant, and received first-rank court dress.

sentences.zh: 時長順年未四十，而戰常陷堅。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Shun was not yet forty years old, yet in battle he constantly plunged into the hard center.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shun was not yet forty, yet he always led the assault himself.

sentences.zh: 每當兵潰時，或抄襲其後，或橫阻其前，俾潰者得整列，以是常轉敗為勝。

translations.literal: Whenever the army collapsed in rout, he either flanked and struck their rear or barred their front crosswise, enabling the routed to form ranks again; by this he often turned defeat into victory.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever his troops broke, he would hit the enemy from the flank or block their front, letting his men reform — and so he often turned defeat into victory.

sentences.zh: 其旗幟尚白，寇望見之，輙呼曰：「小長將軍至矣！

translations.literal: His banners favored white; when bandits saw them they would always cry: The Little General Zhang has come!
translations.idiomatic: His banners were white; rebels who sighted them would cry out: Little General Zhang is here!

sentences.zh: 」相與戒勿犯，其為寇所憚若此。

translations.literal: They would warn one another not to offend him; such was the fear in which bandits held him.
translations.idiomatic: They warned one another not to engage him — such was the dread he inspired.

sentences.zh: 六年，移師蘭州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he moved his army to Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he transferred his command to Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時省城戎備寡，回眾數千突來犯，長順率百人隱小溝，出不意疾擊之，寇愕走，又敗之平番、皋蘭、狄道，既复規取河州，連破太子寺、高家集，被賞賚。

translations.literal: At that time the provincial capital's military preparedness was thin; several thousand Muslims suddenly came to attack; Zhang Shun led a hundred men hidden in a small ditch, struck them unexpectedly in a swift attack, the bandits fled in astonishment; he again defeated them at Pingfan, Gaolan, and Didao; having recovered and planned to take Hezhou, he in succession broke Taizisi and Gaojiaji and received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Lanzhou was thinly garrisoned when several thousand rebels attacked; Zhang Shun hid a hundred men in a ditch, sprang an ambush, and routed them, then defeated them again at Pingfan, Gaolan, and Didao; pressing toward Hezhou he took Taizisi and Gaojiaji in succession and was richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 八年，授鑲紅旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed vice commandant of the Bordered Red Chinese Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made vice commandant of the Bordered Red Chinese Banner.

sentences.zh: 越二年，出署烏里雅蘇台將軍，坐事免。

translations.literal: After two years he went out to serve as acting general of Uliastai, was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he served as acting general of Uliastai but was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，复官，左宗棠調赴甘肅，歷署巴里坤領隊大臣、哈密幫辦大臣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu his office was restored; Zuo Zongtang transferred him to Gansu, and he successively acted as frontier commander at Barkul and assistant commissioner at Hami.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu year two his rank was restored; Zuo Zongtang summoned him to Gansu, where he served as frontier commander at Barkul and assistant commissioner at Hami.

sentences.zh: 初，新疆南路勘界議起，當事者與俄使相持久不決。

translations.literal: At first, when the boundary survey dispute arose on the southern road of Xinjiang, those in charge and the Russian envoy faced each other in stalemate for a long time without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern Xinjiang boundary dispute with Russia arose, negotiations with the Russian envoy dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 至是，長順陟巉岩，披蒙茸，獲見高宗御書界碑，俄使始無異辭，乃定。

translations.literal: At this point Zhang Shun climbed steep cliffs, pushed through thick grass, obtained sight of the boundary stele inscribed by the Gaozong emperor, and the Russian envoy at last had no differing words; it was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shun then climbed rugged cliffs through thick brush, found the boundary stele inscribed by the Qianlong emperor, and the Russians at last raised no objection; the line was fixed.

sentences.zh: 明年，假歸，歷授正白旗漢軍都統、內大臣。

translations.literal: The next year, on leave to return home, he was in succession appointed commandant of the Plain White Chinese Banner and grand minister of the interior.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he went on leave and was appointed in succession commandant of the Plain White Chinese Banner and grand minister of the interior.

sentences.zh: 十四年，出為吉林將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he went out as general of Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was appointed general of Jilin.

sentences.zh: 既蒞事，賑菑荒，維圜法，均釐榷，澄吏治，清盜源，整旗務，境內一切皆治辦。

translations.literal: Once he took office he relieved famine, maintained the currency system, equalized transit duties, clarified official administration, eliminated the sources of banditry, and reorganized banner affairs — everything within the territory was put in order.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he relieved famine, stabilized the currency, equalized transit levies, cleaned up official corruption, cut off banditry at its roots, and reorganized banner administration until the whole province was running properly.

sentences.zh: 又創修吉林通志，書成上之。

translations.literal: He also initiated compilation of the Jilin Gazetteer and, when the work was complete, presented it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He also commissioned a new Jilin provincial gazetteer and presented the finished work to the court.

sentences.zh: 二十年，日軍陷海城，遼陽危。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the Japanese took Haicheng and Liaoyang was in peril.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Guangxu the Japanese captured Haicheng and Liaoyang stood in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 朝命長順往援，節制奉天各軍，並嚴詔：「遼陽有失，唯長順是問。

translations.literal: The court ordered Zhang Shun to go to the rescue, placing all Fengtian armies under his command, with a stern edict: "If Liaoyang is lost, Zhang Shun alone will be held accountable."
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Zhang Shun to the rescue with command over all Fengtian forces, and issued a stern warning: if Liaoyang fell, he alone would answer for it.

sentences.zh: 」時潰軍紛集遼城下，署知州徐慶璋方閉城不令入，軍大閧。

translations.literal: " At that time routed troops crowded beneath Liaoyang's walls; Acting Prefect Xu Qingzhang had closed the gates and would not admit them, and the army raised a great uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Routed troops were massing below the city while Acting Prefect Xu Qingzhang kept the gates shut; the soldiers broke into a furious riot.

sentences.zh: 會長順領百騎至，斬閧者一，餘令還駐沙河。

translations.literal: Just then Zhang Shun arrived leading a hundred horsemen, beheaded one rioter, and ordered the rest to return and encamp at Shahe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shun then arrived with a hundred cavalry, executed one of the ringleaders, and sent the rest back to camp at Shahe.

sentences.zh: 先是長順被命以軍五千分隊應赴，先至者令壁本溪湖，自輕騎入遼陽。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhang Shun had been ordered to march five thousand men in detachments; those who arrived first he ordered to encamp at Benxihu, while he himself entered Liaoyang with a light cavalry escort.
translations.idiomatic: He had been ordered to bring five thousand men in columns; the first detachments he posted at Benxihu while he rode into Liaoyang with only a light escort.

sentences.zh: 亂既定，日軍諜者亦不知其止百騎也，第歸言某將軍至。

translations.literal: Once the disturbance was settled, Japanese spies likewise did not know he had only a hundred horsemen; they merely returned saying a certain general had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, Japanese scouts never learned he had only a hundred horsemen; they reported merely that a general had arrived.

sentences.zh: 日軍遂止弗前，遼陽乃保。

translations.literal: The Japanese then halted and did not advance, and Liaoyang was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese halted their advance, and Liaoyang was saved.

sentences.zh: 已而進攻海城，戰數日弗勝，長順奏趣宋慶會師，詔不許。

translations.literal: Before long he advanced to attack Haicheng; after several days of fighting he could not prevail, and Zhang Shun memorialized urging Song Qing to join forces — the edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He then pushed an attack on Haicheng but failed after several days; he asked the court to hurry Song Qing to join him, and was refused.

sentences.zh: 湘軍將陳湜至，又請劉坤一令合攻，亦未果。

translations.literal: When the Hunan Army general Chen Ti arrived, he again asked Liu Kunyi to order a joint attack — again without success.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiang Army general Chen Ti arrived he again asked Liu Kunyi for a combined assault — again without result.

sentences.zh: 及日軍繞道復攻遼陽，適慶璋守靦峒峪，長順與依克唐阿回援，得無恙。

translations.literal: When the Japanese made a detour to attack Liaoyang again, Xu Qingzhang happened to be defending Miantongyu; Zhang Shun and I Ketang'a returned to the rescue and the city escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: When the Japanese circled back to strike Liaoyang again, Xu Qingzhang was holding Miantongyu; Zhang Shun and I Ketang'a rushed back and the city came through unscathed.

sentences.zh: 和議成，請疾歸。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded he requested leave on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was signed he asked leave on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，復起吉林將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was again appointed general of Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was recalled as general of Jilin.

sentences.zh: 拳亂作，俄羅斯內犯，奉天、黑龍江皆主戰，長順獨持不可。

translations.literal: When the Boxer turmoil arose and Russia invaded from within, Fengtian and Heilongjiang both favored war; Zhang Shun alone held that it should not be fought.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer rising brought Russian invasion, Fengtian and Heilongjiang both urged war; Zhang Shun alone argued against it.

sentences.zh: 又上言拳匪不可恃，東省鐵路隨地皆駐俄兵，宜善為羈縻，寧嚴守以待戰，毋先戰以啟釁。

translations.literal: He further memorialized that the Boxers could not be relied upon, that along the eastern provinces' railways Russian troops were stationed everywhere, that they should be managed with restraint, that it was better to hold firm and await battle than to fight first and provoke hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized further that the Boxers were unreliable, that Russian troops were posted all along the eastern railways, and that the province should hold its lines and wait rather than strike first and provoke war.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其老成持重，奉、吉軍事悉屬之。

translations.literal: The throne praised his seasoned caution and placed all military affairs of Fengtian and Jilin under him.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his seasoned judgment and placed all Fengtian and Jilin military affairs in his hands.

sentences.zh: 戰釁既開，奉、黑皆罹災，而吉林安堵，人服其先見。

translations.literal: Once hostilities had begun, Fengtian and Heilongjiang both suffered disaster, but Jilin remained tranquil, and people acknowledged his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out Fengtian and Heilongjiang were devastated while Jilin stayed calm — proof, people said, of his foresight.

sentences.zh: 日俄之戰，守中立，獨無所犯。

translations.literal: During the Russo-Japanese War he maintained strict neutrality and alone was not violated.
translations.idiomatic: During the Russo-Japanese War he held strictly to neutrality, and his province alone escaped invasion.

sentences.zh: 三十年，卒，贈太子少保，予一等輕車都尉，諡忠靖，入祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he died; he was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the first-class Qingche duwei, posthumous name Zhongjing, and entered for worship in the Temple of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirtieth year, was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and first-class Qingche duwei, given the posthumous name Zhongjing (Loyal and Tranquil), and enshrined in the Temple of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 長順聳幹赬面，鬚眉灑然。

translations.literal: Zhang Shun was tall in stature with a ruddy face and flowing beard and brows.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shun was tall and broad-shouldered, with a ruddy face and a full, imposing beard.

sentences.zh: 富膽略，恆持短矛單騎穿賊陣，為士卒先。

translations.literal: Rich in daring and strategy, he constantly bore a short spear and rode alone through the enemy ranks, going before his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and resourceful, he often rode ahead of his men with a short spear and charged alone through enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 往往以少制眾，以奇制勝，兼謀勇，一時稱良將雲。

translations.literal: He often used the few to overcome the many and the unexpected to win victory, combining strategy and courage — for a time he was acclaimed as a fine general.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly beat larger forces with smaller ones and won by surprise, combining counsel and courage — for a time he was hailed as one of the finest commanders of his day.

sentences.zh: 論曰：中日之戰，淮軍既覆，湘軍隨之，唯豫軍強起支搘。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: In the Sino-Japanese War, after the Huai Army was destroyed the Hunan Army followed suit; only the Henan Army rose with effort to prop up the defense.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: In the Sino-Japanese War the Huai Army was shattered and the Xiang Army followed; only the Henan Army rallied hard to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 慶與玉昆先後失利，亦不復能自振焉。

translations.literal: Song Qing and Yukun suffered defeats in succession and could no longer recover their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qing and Ma Yukun were beaten in turn and never regained their former standing.

sentences.zh: 東三省練軍自成軍後，終未當大敵，而依克唐阿、長順一奮其氣，遂保遼陽而無失，中外稱之。

translations.literal: The trained armies of the three eastern provinces, since their formation, had never faced a great enemy; yet I Ketang'a and Zhang Shun, rousing their spirit once, preserved Liaoyang without loss — Chinese and foreigners alike praised them.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial armies of the northeast had never faced a first-class enemy since their creation, yet I Ketang'a and Zhang Shun, rallying their men once, held Liaoyang without loss — a feat praised at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 喪師辱國者數矣，此固差強人意者哉。

translations.literal: There had been many occasions of armies lost and the nation shamed; this was at least somewhat satisfying to men's minds.
translations.idiomatic: The empire had suffered humiliating defeats again and again; this, at least, was something a man could take some comfort in.
